idiom_name: toJSON() + JSON.parse(reviver), or a toPlain()/fromPlain() function pair
implementation_notes: JavaScript needs neither an interface nor a registry: JSON.stringify calls value.toJSON(key) when it exists, and JSON.parse accepts a reviver that rebuilds values while parsing, so the two directions live in two duck-typed hooks that sit in the same module. Where JSON is not involved, the same shape is a pair of plain functions (toDTO/fromDTO) or a static fromPlain next to an instance toPlain. The classic converter class with two abstract methods is replaced by these hooks and only reappears when converters must be selected dynamically, for example a registry keyed by format name.
pitfalls: A JSON round trip preserves no class identity: prototypes, undefined values, functions, Map/Set and Date objects do not survive, so only the explicit reviver or fromJSON rebuilds them.
JSON.stringify throws on BigInt and drops undefined properties, so a missing required field reappears as undefined rather than as an error.
The reviver runs bottom-up - children before their parent - so a parent hook receives already-transformed children and must not assume raw shapes.
Parsing untrusted JSON and copying it into objects enables prototype pollution through __proto__ keys, and calling JSON.stringify inside toJSON recurses forever.
